transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

Some moisture is normal on a Bosch Serie 4, especially if it uses condensation drying rather than a heated drying element. Plastic tubs are the worst: they do not retain heat, so water does not evaporate from them well. A few drops on glasses can also be normal.

But items should not generally come out soaking wet every cycle. Things to check:

• Fill the rinse-aid reservoir. Bosch machines rely heavily on rinse aid for drying. Increase the rinse-aid setting by one or two steps if glasses are still covered in droplets.
• Use a hotter/longer programme. Eco cycles and short cycles often dry less well. Try Auto, Intensive, or a programme with Extra Dry / ExtraDry enabled, if your exact model has it.
• Open the door slightly at the end of the programme, once it has finished, to let steam escape. Some models do this automatically; if yours does not, it can make a big difference.
• Unload the lower basket first. Water pooled on mugs or plastic items in the top rack can drip onto everything below.
• Angle plastic tubs and cups downward and avoid nesting them. Make sure nothing is collecting water on its base.
• Check the detergent/rinse-aid combination. Even with all-in-one tablets, separate rinse aid is often still needed, particularly in hard-water areas.
• Clean the filter and check spray arms if washing performance is also poor.

If this is a new change and ceramic plates, metal pans, and glassware are all very wet even after a hot cycle with rinse aid, it may point to a heating or drying-system issue, and Bosch service or the retailer may need to inspect it.

If you can share the full model number (usually starting `SMS`, `SMV`, `SPV`, etc.) and which programme you use, I can tell you what drying options that specific Serie 4 should have.
Thanks. I use Eco 50 every time, and the rinse aid symbol is lit so it's empty - I only use all-in-one tablets. I also open the door straight away when it finishes. Should I fill the rinse aid?

Yes — fill the rinse-aid dispenser, even if you use all-in-one tablets.

On Bosch dishwashers, rinse aid makes a substantial difference to drying because it helps water sheet off glass and dishes instead of forming droplets. It is particularly helpful on Eco 50 and for plastics, which naturally dry poorly.

What to do:

1. Buy dishwasher rinse aid (any reputable brand is fine).
2. Open the dispenser on the inside of the door and fill it to the max line.
3. If your model lets you adjust the dosage, start around the middle setting (often 3 or 4).
4. Run a few normal cycles before judging the result; the dispenser may take a little time to settle.

If you then see streaks, a bluish film, or excess foaming, turn the rinse-aid setting down. If you still get lots of droplets, increase it one level.

Opening the door at the end is helpful, but opening it immediately can release steam before it has condensed and drained off the cooler stainless-steel interior. For best results, try leaving it closed for around 15–30 minutes after the programme ends, then open it slightly or fully. That said, with rinse aid added, you should still see an improvement either way.

Plastic tubs may still retain some water or need a quick shake/hand-dry — that part is normal for condensation-drying machines.
